properties.title: Alameda
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Sea level rise threatens the entirety of Alameda’s shoreline and Bay Farm Island
  • Groundwater rise may impact legacy contamination at Alameda Point
Highlights
  • The Oakland Alameda Adaptation Committee (OAAC) is creating a plan to protect the city for up to 5.5ft of sea level rise
Opportunities
  • Continue to advance the long-term shoreline adaptation plan and the associated near-term projects. This will preserve community resources like the Robert W Crown Memorial Beach, new development on Alameda Point, and economic centers like the South Shore Shopping Center.
  • Invest in a Workforce Development program to build and maintain green infrastructure across the city.

properties.title: Albany
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Sea level and groundwater rise by 2100 will flood parts of the Albany bulb, the area around Golden Gate Fields, and the Tom Bates Regional Sports Complex
  • Transportation infrastructure near the shoreline is at risk like Amtrak and highway I-580
Highlights
  • Albany is coordinating a shoreline adaptation plan with Berkeley and Emeryville
Opportunities
  • Create a storm drain master plan that aligns with Albany’s green infrastructure plan to ensure the storm drain system can function under future conditions.
  • Implement a Sea Level Rise Overlay Zone where flooding will occur to ensure infrastructure is built to be resilient.

properties.title: American Canyon
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Flooding along the Napa River and shoreline
  • Flood risk to the wastewater treatment plant, Public Works Yard, and pump stations along Wetlands Edge Road
Highlights
  • American Canyon partnered with other jurisdictions in Napa County to create a joint Regional Climate Action and Adaptation Plan, and is now working to create a Regional Shoreline Adaptation Plan
Opportunities
  • Create a groundwater rise plan that assesses risk to underground utilities, contaminated sites, and flood-prone areas.
  • Create a green stormwater infrastructure (GSI) plan to ensure new city infrastructure incorporates GSI wherever possible.

properties.title: Belmont
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Areas east of the Caltrain line at risk of flooding from 3.3 feet of sea level rise
  • Flooding along Belmont Creek during storms
Highlights
  • The Belmont Creek Restoration Project will increase the creek’s flood retention capacity while restoring native vegetation
Opportunities
  • Establish design standards to ensure new developments and infrastructure are resilient to future flood risk.
  • Create a Storm Drain Master Plan that ensures that the city-owned portion of the storm drain system has the capacity to function under future flood conditions.

properties.title: Belvedere
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Flooding of the Belvedere Lagoon, shoreline neighborhoods, and San Rafael Avenue, the primary access road to Belvedere
Highlights
  • Belvedere is upgrading its coastal flood barriers to protect the city from rising sea levels and severe storms
Opportunities
  • Update adaptation plans and design flood barriers to be adaptable to 6.6 feet of sea level rise.
  • Create a green stormwater infrastructure plan.

properties.title: Benicia
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Flooding of the Benicia Marina, residential areas in lower Downtown Benicia, parts of the Valero Refinery, and parts of the Benicia Industrial Park
  • Movement of contamination from toxic sites near the shoreline
Highlights
  • Design of a sea wall to protect the wastewater treatment plant from sea level rise
  • Collaboration with other Solano County entities to create a Regional Shoreline Adaptation Plan
Opportunities
  • Incorporate wetland restoration and nature-based solutions in shoreline protections wherever possible.
  • Establish resilient design standards – such as requiring new buildings to be elevated above projected flood levels – to ensure homes, businesses, and infrastructure are resilient to future flood risk.

properties.title: Berkeley
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Inundation from sea level rise and groundwater rise along the Berkeley shoreline inland to San Pablo Ave
  • Increased stormwater runoff will back up storm drains, causing roadways and sidewalks to flood
Highlights
  • Berkeley is working on their shoreline adaptation in conjunction with the cities of Emeryville, Albany, and Oakland
Opportunities
  • Implement proposed policy goals in the Stormwater Master Plan Update.
  • Implementing a Sea Level Rise Overlay Zone in an appropriate area would ensure infrastructure is built to be resilient to flooding.

properties.title: Brisbane
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Downtown Brisbane, Northwest Bayshore, and Tunnel Ave are vulnerable to groundwater rise and sea level rise
  • The Brisbane Baylands will be inundated by sea level rise
Highlights
  • The Brisbane Lagoon Watershed Sea Level Rise Adaptation Plan
Opportunities
  • Adopt OneShoreline’s guidelines for a Sea Level Rise Overlay District to ensure new development is resilient in the face of future flooding.
  • Update the Storm Drain Master Plan to ensure Brisbane’s storm drain infrastructure can function under future flood conditions.

properties.title: Burlingame
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Flooding in most of the Bayfront Area and parts of Rollins Road
Highlights
  • The Sea Level Rise Overlay District which establishes public access and sea level rise building standards for new developments
Opportunities
  • Establish building standards to protect against groundwater rise – such as requiring developments near contaminated sites to establish contaminant monitoring plans.
  • Update the Storm Drain Master Plan to ensure that the storm drain system can function under future climate conditions.

properties.title: Corte Madera
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Severe flooding in the Mariner Cove and Marina Village neighborhoods
  • Permanent inundation of marshes in the Corte Madera Ecological Reserve
Highlights
  • Regulations making it easier for homeowners to raise their homes above expected flood levels
Opportunities
  • Establish design standards to ensure new developments and infrastructure are resilient to future flood risk.
  • Maximize opportunities for nature-based flood resilience and marsh restoration in the city's ongoing flood berm upgrade planning.

properties.title: East Palo Alto
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Flooding along San Francisquito Creek and the shoreline
  • Contaminated sites along the shoreline
Highlights
  • The SAFER Bay Project, designed by the San Francisquito Creek JPA, will guard against 3.5 feet of sea level rise
Opportunities
  • Establish building design standards in at-risk areas to ensure new buildings are flood-resilient and to protect renters and homeowners in disadvantaged communities.
  • Work with community-based organizations and regulatory agencies to support the cleanup of contaminated sites. Community groups like PACT, YUCA, and Climate Resilient Communities are actively calling for the cleanup of specific sites due to the threat of future flooding.

properties.title: Emeryville
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Flooding on Powell Street, cutting off emergency routes, and flooding of commercial and industrial areas
  • Permanent inundation of salt marshes
Highlights
  • The East Bay Crescent Shoreline Project, which will include an ecotone levee in the Emeryville Crescent Marsh to protect the city from 5.5 ft of sea level rise
Opportunities
  • Develop strategies to address groundwater rise impacts on shoreline projects, vulnerable neighborhoods and infrastructure, the storm drain system, and contaminated sites on the shoreline.
  • Establish resilient design standards to ensure new developments and infrastructure are resilient to future flood risk.

properties.title: Foster City
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Groundwater rise will create new flood risks throughout the city
  • Sea level rise conditions over 3ft will top the recently raised levee surrounding the city
Highlights
  • Foster City's support of the San Mateo County Flood and Sea Level Rise Resiliency District, OneShoreline
Opportunities
  • Create a Storm Drain Master Plan to ensure storm drains can function under increased precipitation and higher groundwater level conditions.
  • Have standardized development codes for rising groundwater conditions.

properties.title: Fremont
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Flooding along the shoreline in Ardenwood Technology Park, the Coyote Hills/Ardenwood neighborhoods, and the Baylands Industrial Area
  • Localized flooding along creeks and near the base of the hills
Highlights
  • The Coyote Hills Restoration Project preserved over 300 acres of tidal marsh habitat
Opportunities
  • Collaborate with Union City and Newark to create a Regional Shoreline Adaptation Plan.
  • Create a Storm Drain Master Plan that ensures that the storm drain system has the capacity to function under future flood conditions.

properties.title: Hayward
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Flooding of industrial, commercial, and residential areas on the shoreline and along creeks and drainageways
  • Flooding of wetlands like the Oro Loma Marsh and Hayward Marsh
Highlights
  • The Hayward Regional Shoreline Adaptation Master Plan (HRSAP), which recommends nature-based strategies for preparing for sea level rise
  • The First Mile Horizontal Levee flood resilience and water treatment project
Opportunities
  • Establish design standards to ensure new developments and infrastructure are resilient to future flood risk.
  • Create a Storm Drain Master Plan that ensures that the city-owned portion of the storm drain system has the capacity to function under future flood conditions.

properties.title: Hercules
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Increased flooding along Pinole Creek and Refugio Creek
  • Sea level rise risk to the Hercules Hub, a planned multi-use development
Highlights
  • The Refugio Creek Overlay Zone, which preserves the land near Refugio Creek for flood protection and open space
Opportunities
  • Consider multiple sea level rise scenarios in the city’s resilience planning, including the possibility of 6.6 feet of sea level rise and related groundwater rise by 2100.
  • Establish resilient design standards to ensure new developments and infrastructure are resilient to future flood risk.

properties.title: Larkspur
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Flooding of residential areas along Corte Madera Creek, including some of the county’s limited affordable housing
  • Movement of contamination from toxic sites along the shoreline
Highlights
  • Larkspur has designated Shoreline/Wetland Conservation Areas that are preserved for habitat and recreation
Opportunities
  • Partner with Marin County and neighboring cities to create a Regional Shoreline Adaptation Plan.
  • Explore policies that would allow homeowners to raise their homes above the projected sea level rise flood levels.

properties.title: Martinez
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Sea level rise could inundate the public wastewater treatment plant
  • Transportation infrastructure near the shoreline is at risk like the Amtrak station and Bay Trail
Highlights
  • Martinez participates in the Resilient Shoreline Coalition with Contra Costa County and other shoreline cities
Opportunities
  • Expand green infrastructure requirements to the public right of way for conditions of approval in new developments and alignment with a Storm Drain Master Plan.
  • Implement a Sea Level Rise Overlay Zone where flooding will occur to ensure resilient infrastructure.

properties.title: Menlo Park
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Flooding along San Francisquito Creek and in the Belle Haven and Bayfront neighborhoods
  • Movement of contamination from toxic sites along the shoreline into surrounding communities
Highlights
  • The SAFER Bay Project, designed by the San Francisquito Creek JPA, will guard against 3.5 feet of sea level rise
Opportunities
  • Establish building design standards in at-risk areas to ensure new buildings are flood-resilient and to protect renters and homeowners in disadvantaged communities
  • Work with community-based organizations and regulatory agencies to support the cleanup of contaminated sites. Community groups like PACT, YUCA, and Climate Resilient Communities are actively calling for the cleanup of specific sites due to the threat of future flooding

properties.title: Mill Valley
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • More severe and frequent flooding in Shelter Bay and Tam Junction
  • Permanent inundation of Bothin Marsh
Highlights
  • The Mill Valley Shoreline Adaptation Framework will be a road map for protecting residents from the impacts of future flooding.
Opportunities
  • Implement a Sea Level Rise Overlay District to ensure any new development is able to withstand sea level rise and related flood risks.
  • Update the Storm Drain Master Plan to ensure Mill Valley’s storm drain infrastructure can function under future flood conditions.

properties.title: Millbrae
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Flooding in areas east of the BART tracks, including residential neighborhoods, roads, and the wastewater treatment plant
  • Extreme storms may overwhelm the storm drain system
Highlights
  • Millbrae partnered with OneShoreline and Burlingame to design a shoreline resilience project to protect the city from sea level rise
  • Millbrae has created several multi-benefit green street projects that improve road safety while treating stormwater runoff and reducing flooding
Opportunities
  • Establish resilient design standards – such as requiring new buildings to be elevated above projected flood levels – to ensure homes, businesses, and infrastructure are resilient to future flood risk.
  • Incorporate nature-based solutions into the Millbrae and Burlingame Shoreline Resilience Project as much as possible.

properties.title: Mountain View
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Flooding north of Highway 101, including the North Bayshore Area
Highlights
  • Mountain View’s Sea Level Rise Capital Improvement Plan identifies 12 sea level rise resilience projects to protect from flooding along the shoreline and creeks
  • A former salt pond adjacent to Mountain View’s Shoreline Park was recently restored to wetland habitat
Opportunities
  • Establish resilient design standards – such as requiring new buildings to be elevated above projected flood levels – to ensure homes, businesses, and infrastructure are resilient to future flood risk.
  • Update the city’s flood resilience project designs to accommodate 6.6 feet of sea level rise and groundwater rise.

properties.title: Newark
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Flooding of wetlands and neighborhoods along the shoreline
  • Localized flooding on inland streets during extreme storms
Highlights
  • Newark’s Flood Modeling Report creates a holistic understanding of flood risk and the combined effects of sea level rise, groundwater rise, and climate-driven storms
Opportunities
  • Newark should preserve and restore its wetlands and prioritize transferring Area 4 to the Don Edwards National Wildlife Refuge.
  • Newark should collaborate with Union City and Fremont to create a Regional Shoreline Resilience Plan.

properties.title: Novato
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Permanent inundation of the Hamilton Wetlands
  • More frequent and severe flooding of the Oaks Shopping Center and neighborhoods like Hamilton and Bahia
Highlights
  • Novato’s comprehensive vulnerability analysis that can be used to inform future sea level rise planning
Opportunities
  • Adopt a Sea Level Rise Overlay District to ensure any new development is built to withstand inundation from sea level rise, stormwater flooding, and emergent groundwater.
  • Create a Green Infrastructure Plan with a framework for multi-benefit green stormwater infrastructure implementation to improve flood control and water quality.

properties.title: Oakland
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Flooding in low-income neighborhoods and communities of color in the flatlands of West and East Oakland
  • Flooding of contaminated sites in West and East Oakland
Highlights
  • An updated Storm Drain Master Plan in progress to ensure the storm drain system can accommodate more extreme storms
  • The Oakland Alameda Adaptation Committee (OAAC), which is creating a plan to protect the Oakland-Alameda Estuary shoreline from up to 5.5ft of sea level rise
Opportunities
  • Establish design standards to ensure new developments and infrastructure are resilient to future flood risk.
  • Work with community members and regulatory agencies to prioritize and support the cleanup of contaminated sites that may pose a health risk to vulnerable communities when groundwater levels rise.

properties.title: Palo Alto
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Regular flooding of 4,000 homes and 14 miles of evacuation routes
  • Permanent inundation of wetlands in the Palo Alto Baylands
Highlights
  • The Palo Alto Living Levee Project, which will provide habitat, flood protection, and water quality benefits
Opportunities
  • Establish design standards to ensure new developments and infrastructure are resilient to future flood risk.
  • Monitor contaminated sites to ensure that pollutants are not travelling into nearby neighborhoods through sewer pipes.

properties.title: Petaluma
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Overflow of the Petaluma River caused by sea level rise will flood neighborhoods like Historic Downtown Petaluma and wildlife habitat like the River Baylands
  • Larger King Tides will flood southern portions of southern Petaluma, including sections of Lakeview Street
Highlights
  • Petaluma’s General Plan update will require planning for future flooding conditions
Opportunities
  • Planning for groundwater rise should be incorporated into future flood planning along with sea level rise and stormwater flooding.
  • A Green Infrastructure Plan would help prevent stormwater flooding and provide co-benefits.

properties.title: Pinole
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Flooding in neighborhoods along Pinole Creek
Highlights
  • The Pinole Creek Greenway Master Plan, which describes multi-benefit flood resilience and habitat restoration projects
Opportunities
  • Ensure that flood control plans for Pinole Creek account for future storms, which may become more frequent and extreme due to climate change.
  • Consider partnering with the City of Hercules to move forward with the Chelsea Wetlands restoration project, which is currently on hold.

properties.title: Redwood City
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Inundation of coastal developments like Redwood Shores
  • Flooding of Bair Island
Highlights
  • Redwood City’s Sea Level Rise Vulnerability Assessment and participation in OneShoreline, a collaborative effort between all San Mateo County cities to plan for sea level rise.
Opportunities
  • Utilize nature-based solutions as a part of the upcoming Redwood Shores Sea Level Rise Protection Project.
  • Update the Storm Drain Master Plan to ensure that Redwood City’s storm drain infrastructure can function under future flood conditions.

properties.title: Richmond
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Flooding of neighborhoods along Wildcat Creek, San Pablo Creek, and the shoreline, including low-income communities such as the Coronado and Santa Fe neighborhoods
  • Movement of contaminants from toxic sites into surrounding communities
Highlights
  • Richmond has begun working on a Sea Level Rise Adaptation and Resiliency Plan
  • The Richmond Bay Specific Plan requires the development area to be raised 1 foot above the projected flood level at 3 feet of sea level rise
Opportunities
  • Establish design standards – such as requiring new buildings to be elevated above projected flood levels – to ensure new developments and infrastructure are resilient to future flood risk.
  • Work with community organizations and regulatory agencies to support the cleanup of contaminated sites that may pose a health risk when groundwater levels rise.

properties.title: San Bruno
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Flooding in residential areas east of the Caltrain line between 1st and 7th streets
Highlights
  • San Bruno is updating its Storm Drainage Master Plan
  • The San Bruno Creek Flood Zone Project will engage community members to design a nature-based flood resilience project for San Bruno Creek
Opportunities
  • Establish design standards – such as requiring new buildings to be elevated above projected flood levels – to ensure new developments and infrastructure are resilient to future flood risk.
  • As part of the Storm Drainage Master Plan update, study where flooding will intensify due to more extreme rainfall resulting from climate change.

properties.title: San Carlos
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Flooding along Pulgas Creek, Cordilleras Creek, and Belmont Creek
  • Flooding of shoreline assets including residential neighborhoods, Highway 101, and the San Carlos Airport
Highlights
  • San Carlos has committed to creating its own Regional Shoreline Adaptation Plan (RSAP) to comply with state mandates.
Opportunities
  • Establish resilient design standards to ensure new developments and infrastructure are resilient to future flood risk. These could expand on existing sea level rise design standards for the Northeast Area neighborhood.
  • Study which areas will flood more frequently due to future storms and update the city’s flood resilience plans accordingly.

properties.title: San Francisco
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Flooding along the Embarcadero and low-lying creek-adjacent neighborhoods like Mission Bay and Bayview-Hunters Point
Highlights
  • Shoreline resilience and open space projects like the India Basin Waterfront Park Project
Opportunities
  • Implementing a Sea Level Rise Overlay Zone to ensure infrastructure is built to be resilient to flooding.
  • Establish a 100-foot buffer along creek banks for flood protection.

properties.title: San Jose
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Flooding in the Alviso neighborhood
  • Flooding along the Guadalupe River and Coyote Creek
Highlights
  • The Climate Adaptation and Resilience Plan, which is being created and will outline strategies to reduce the risk of climate-related disasters
Opportunities
  • Identify areas at risk of flooding from groundwater rise and integrate this analysis into the city’s ongoing flood protection projects.
  • Continue participating in the “Healthy Watersheds Thriving Communities” initiative, which is working to identify multi-benefit, community-informed green infrastructure projects. Once priority projects are identified, focus on funding and building these projects.

properties.title: San Leandro
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Flooding along the shoreline and San Leandro Creek, impacting a wastewater treatment plant, parks, railroad lines, and roads
  • Flooding and erosion of wetlands, beaches, and the Bay Trail
Opportunities
  • Establish design standards – such as requiring new buildings to be elevated above projected flood levels – to ensure new developments and infrastructure are resilient to future flood risk.
  • Update the Storm Drain Master Plan to account for the compounding impacts of sea level rise, groundwater rise, and more extreme storms.

properties.title: San Mateo
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Flooding of 21 miles of highway, 83 miles of local roads at risk, 68 acres of wetlands, and homes and businesses
  • Flooding of contaminated sites near the shoreline
Highlights
  • Levee improvements to protect the North Shoreview neighborhood
  • Complete green street projects like the Laurel Elementary Safe Green Streets project and the Humboldt Sustainable Street improvements
Opportunities
  • Develop strategies to address groundwater rise impacts on shoreline projects, vulnerable neighborhoods and infrastructure, the storm drain system, and contaminated sites.
  • Establish resilient design standards to ensure new developments and infrastructure are resilient to future flood risk.

properties.title: San Rafael
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Flooding along the shoreline and San Rafael Creek, including severe flooding in the Canal area, a densely populated majority-Latino neighborhood
Highlights
  • The Nuestro Canal, Nuestro Futuro project, led by the community-based organization Canal Alliance, will identify community-supported flood resilience strategies for the Canal neighborhood
Opportunities
  • Create a Storm Drain Master Plan that ensures the storm drain system is prepared to accommodate the compounding impacts of sea level rise, groundwater rise, and more extreme storms.
  • Establish design standards – such as requiring new buildings to be elevated above projected flood levels – to ensure new developments and infrastructure are resilient to future flood risk.

properties.title: Santa Clara
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Flooding of low-lying areas in northern Santa Clara near Highway 237
  • Flooding in neighborhoods along San Tomas Aquino Creek
Highlights
  • Santa Clara plans to join Santa Clara County’s countywide regional shoreline adaptation planning effort.
Opportunities
  • Consider multiple sea level rise scenarios in the city’s Regional Shoreline Adaptation Plan, including the possibility of 6.6 feet of sea level rise by 2100.
  • Update the city’s storm drain and flood resilience plans to ensure it can withstand future storm conditions.

properties.title: Sausalito
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Frequent flooding in Downtown Sausalito
  • Permanent inundation of transportation infrastructure like the ferry terminal, bus stops, and Bridgeway street
Highlights
  • Sausalito’s Shoreline Adaptation Plan, which plans for groundwater rise, stormwater, and sea level rise flooding
Opportunities
  • Adopt a Sea Level Rise Overlay District to ensure new development is resilient in the face of future flooding.
  • Create a Green Infrastructure Plan to integrate nature-based flood solutions into city infrastructure planning and meet flood resilience goals.

properties.title: South San Francisco
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Flooding of the Lindenville neighborhood and areas along Colma Creek
  • Flooding of the South San Francisco - San Bruno Water Quality Control Plant
Highlights
  • The Sea Level Rise Overlay District which establishes public access and sea level rise building standards for new developments
Opportunities
  • Establish a Groundwater Rise Overlay District to build upon the Sea Level Rise Overlay District and ensure that residents are protected from future emergent groundwater threats.
  • Update the city’s Storm Drain Master Plan to ensure that the storm drain infrastructure can function under future flood conditions.

properties.title: Suisun City
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Flooding in the Downtown Waterfront Area, some residential areas south of Highway 12, and some areas along Laurel Creek and Pennsylvania Avenue Creek
Highlights
  • A 2022 Community Resilience Building Workshop identified the city’s top climate vulnerabilities and engaged the community to identify actions to address them
  • Suisun City will participate in Solano County’s multijurisdictional Regional Shoreline Adaptation Plan
Opportunities
  • Incorporate nature-based solutions into the city’s flood protections as much as possible, and preserve the wetlands that border the city.
  • Establish design standards – such as requiring new buildings to be elevated above projected flood levels – to ensure new developments and infrastructure are resilient to future flood risk.

properties.title: Sunnyvale
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Flooding in the Moffet Park neighborhood
  • Flooding of city’s wastewater treatment plant
Highlights
  • The Ecological Innovation District, an area of the Moffet Park neighborhood designated for sustainable and ecologically resilient development practices
Opportunities
  • Establish resilient design standards to ensure new developments and infrastructure are resilient to future flood risk. These can expand upon existing design standards in the Ecological Innovation District.
  • Develop an equity framework that identifies areas of overlapping vulnerabilities (such as extreme heat, flooding, and socioeconomic vulnerabilities) to determine where to prioritize climate adaptations.

properties.title: Tiburon
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Flooding of the ferry terminal, Bay Trail, and Highway 101
  • Flooding of Tiburon’s fire department, library, and post office
Highlights
  • The Sea Level Rise and Shoreline Adaptation Plan, which plans to protect against 6.5 feet of sea level rise
Opportunities
  • Adopt a Sea Level Rise Overlay District to ensure new development is resilient in the face of future flooding.
  • Update the Storm Drain Master Plan to ensure Tiburon’s storm drain infrastructure can function under future flood conditions.

properties.title: Union City
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Flooding in industrial, commercial, and residential areas along the shoreline and creek channels
  • Flooding of the Alvarado Wastewater Treatment Plant
Highlights
  • The city is updating its Climate Action Plan, which will include sea level rise adaptation strategies.
Opportunities
  • Partner with the neighboring cities of Fremont and Newark to create a Regional Shoreline Adaptation Plan to comply with state mandates.
  • Establish building design standards in at-risk areas to ensure new buildings are flood resilient.

properties.title: Vallejo
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Flooding of the White Slough, South Vallejo, and Mare Island neighborhoods which will impact residential and commercial areas, unhoused residents, and the wastewater treatment plant
Highlights
  • Vallejo will participate in Solano County’s multijurisdictional Regional Shoreline Adaptation Plan
  • Developments in areas vulnerable to 55 inches of sea level rise are required to conduct an environmental review and identify flood mitigation measures
Opportunities
  • Nature-based flood protections and wetland preservation should be incorporated into the ongoing plans to redevelop Mare Island.
  • Vallejo should strengthen its existing flood resilience standards to require all new developments vulnerable to 6.6 feet of sea level rise to incorporate flood-resilient measures such as elevating the first flood above projected flood levels.

properties.title: Alameda County
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Flooding from sea level rise and groundwater rise, including in the unincorporated community of San Lorenzo
  • Inland flooding from stormwater in communities like Castro Valley
Highlights
  • The Eden Landing wetland restoration project will restore 6,400 acres of tidal marsh for flood protection and habitat creation
Opportunities
  • Support and collaborate with cities in their shoreline adaptation plan efforts
  • Study the flood risk implications of future rainfall projections to ensure residents and infrastructure are protected

properties.title: Contra Costa County
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Groundwater rise in shoreline communities threatens to inundate contaminated sites, posing a public health risk
  • Sea level rise threatens shoreline areas like the Crocket/Carquinez Bridge landing and unincorporated areas like the Rodeo and Bay Point neighborhoods
Highlights
  • Contra Costa County is creating a collaborative shoreline resilience plan to protect city and county assets and residents
Opportunities
  • Study the impacts of flooding on contaminated sites around the county to protect residents from harmful health outcomes
  • Establish building design standards in at-risk areas to ensure new buildings are flood-resilient

properties.title: Marin County
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Flooding of critical transportation routes such as Highway 37 and the Manzanita Interchange of US Highways 101 and 1
  • Flooding of 12,000 buildings, several wastewater treatment plants, and ecological assets like the Novato Baylands and Bothin Marsh
Highlights
  • The County hired a Chief Climate Officer, a new position tasked with advancing the county’s sea level rise response
  • The Evolving Shorelines project will restore Bothin Marsh to help it adapt to sea level rise and protect inland assets from flooding
Opportunities
  • Provide countywide coordination among cities and agencies for sea level rise resilience planning
  • Create stormwater plans for the county’s unincorporated urban areas to prepare them for future storm conditions

properties.title: Napa County
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Environmental assets like the American Canyon Wetlands could be lost to sea level rise and groundwater rise
  • Unincorporated communities like Cuttings Wharf, Brazos, and Buchli are all at risk of inundation
Highlights
  • Napa County is coordinating with the city of American Canyon on a Shoreline Adaptation Plan
Opportunities
  • Establish building design standards in at-risk areas to ensure new buildings are flood-resilient
  • Study how future rainfall projections impact flood risk and ensure that the storm drain system can accommodate more intense storms

properties.title: San Mateo County
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Sea level rise, groundwater rise, and liquefaction threaten areas that were built on top of low-lying bay fill, such Foster City and Redwood Shores
  • Public assets including 34 schools, 2 airports and 5 wastewater treatment plants are vulnerable to sea level rise
Highlights
  • San Mateo County’s Sea Level Rise Resiliency Planning District (OneShoreline) is created flood resilience planning guidance for the cities and is coordinating cohesive flood protections for the Bay shoreline
Opportunities
  • As rising sea levels push the groundwater table higher, contaminated sites may be flooded from below and allow vaporized toxins to enter buildings through sewer pipes. OneShoreline should create guidance for upgrading sewer infrastructure to address this risk
  • OneShoreline should prioritize nature-based solutions in sea level rise adaptation projects

properties.title: Santa Clara County
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Flooding along the shoreline in northern Santa Clara County, including the unincorporated area of Moffett Field
  • Flooding along Coyote Creek, Calabasas Creek, Guadalupe River, and other creeks as extreme storms increase
Highlights
  • Santa Clara County is coordinating with all of its shoreline cities to create a countywide Regional Shoreline Adaptation Plan
  • The South Bay Shoreline Project will combine wetland restoration with FEMA-certified levees to protect against sea level rise
Opportunities
  • Identify contaminated sites that are at risk of flooding and work with property owners to implement climate adaptation plans to protect community health
  • Pursue funding and implementing green stormwater infrastructure projects identified as part of the county’s ongoing “Healthy Watersheds, Thriving Communities” initiative

properties.title: Solano County
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Contaminated sites along the shoreline, specifically in Fairfield and Suisun City, may be inundated by groundwater rise
  • Suisun Marsh could become permanently inundated by sea level rise
Highlights
  • The Solano Bayshore Resiliency Project will create a collaborative sea level rise plan for the county, Benicia, Fairfield, Suisun City, Vallejo, and the Fairfield-Suisun Sewer District
Opportunities
  • Study the impacts of sea level rise on contaminated sites and the potential health risks to surrounding communities
  • Establish building design standards in at-risk areas to ensure new buildings are resilient to flooding

properties.title: Sonoma County
properties.description:
Key Vulnerabilities
  • Increased storms and sea level rise will cause more extreme flooding along the Russian River
  • Sea level rise threatens county medical, transportation, energy, and emergency service resources near the shoreline
Highlights
  • Sonoma County is collaborating with the City of Petaluma to create the Sonoma County North Bay Sea Level Rise Resilience Plan
Opportunities
  • Create a Storm Drain Master Plan to ensure county storm drains can function under future storm conditions
  • Create a Green Infrastructure Plan to mitigate stormwater flooding using urban greening features
